title: Classical configuration, phase and reference spaces

items.title: Classical configuration, cotangent phase and reference measures
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the exact choice strength required by
[[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]] to construct the smooth
cotangent manifold. Let $d,N\ge1$, let $Q$ be a smooth $d$-manifold, and
choose a countable smooth-chart subcover of its atlas. Such a subcover is
obtained from a countable basis of the second-countable topology by choosing,
for each basis element contained in a chart domain, one such chart domain; this
countable selection is covered by the stated Axiom of Countable Choice. Give
$Q_N:=Q^N$ the product topology and the product smooth structure generated by
the charts
$$\left(U_1\times\cdots\times U_N,\ (q_1,\ldots,q_N)\mapsto(\phi_1(q_1),\ldots,\phi_N(q_N))\right),$$
where each $(U_i,\phi_i)$ belongs to the chosen countable subcover of charts of
$Q$. These images are open in $\mathbb R^{dN}$, and their transition maps are
componentwise smooth, so they form a smooth atlas of dimension $n=dN$; the
finite product of the countable chart family is countable. Its generated
maximal atlas is the product smooth structure in the convention of
[[def-smooth-manifold]]. The induced cotangent charts are indexed by these
base charts and form a countable atlas of $\Gamma_N$. Its
**configuration space** is $Q_N$. Its **phase space** is the cotangent bundle
$$\Gamma_N:=T^*Q_N,$$
whose points are pairs $(q,p)$ with $p\in T_q^*Q_N$. Let
$\pi_N:T^*Q_N\to Q_N$ be the cotangent-bundle projection. The **tautological
one-form** and **canonical symplectic form** are
$$\lambda_{(q,p)}(\xi):=p(d\pi_N\xi),\qquad \omega_N:=-d\lambda.$$
Thus in an induced cotangent chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$,
$$\lambda=\sum_{j=1}^n p_j\,dq^j,\qquad \omega_N=\sum_{j=1}^n dq^j\wedge dp_j.$$
The cotangent supplier proves $\omega_N$ closed and nondegenerate under the
same Countable Choice premise. On an open phase chart this is exactly the
standard form of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]];
[[lem-cm-standard-symplectic-form-is-closed-and-nondegenerate]] gives its
closedness, contraction and nondegeneracy coordinate calculations.

Let $\mathcal F_N:=\mathcal B(\Gamma_N)$ be the Borel sigma-algebra generated
by the topology of $\Gamma_N$ ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). The **Liouville
density**, denoted
$$d\Lambda_N:=|\omega_N^{\wedge n}|/n!,$$
is the positive density whose coordinate density in every induced cotangent
chart is $dq^1\cdots dq^n\,dp_1\cdots dp_n$. Define its Borel measure
$\Lambda_N$ explicitly as follows. If $\Gamma_N=\varnothing$,
set $\Lambda_N(\varnothing)=0$. Otherwise choose an at-most-countable induced
cotangent atlas $(V_k,\psi_k)_{k\in J}$ indexed by $J\subseteq\mathbb N$, order
$J$ by the usual order, and set
$$E_k:=V_k\setminus\bigcup_{j\in J,\,j<k}V_j\quad(k\in J).$$
For $A\in\mathcal F_N$, put
$$\Lambda_N(A):=\sum_{k\in J}\lambda_{2n}\bigl(\psi_k(A\cap E_k)\bigr),$$
where $\lambda_{2n}$ is Lebesgue measure on the chart image. Each $E_k$ is
Borel, and each chart map is a homeomorphism, so the terms are defined on
Borel sets. The coordinate transitions preserve $\omega_N$ because
$\omega_N=-d\lambda$ is intrinsic; hence they preserve $\omega_N^n/n!$
and have absolute Jacobian one. For two atlases, the intersections of their
disjoint chart pieces form a countable common Borel refinement. On each
nonempty refinement piece the coordinate transition is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism
with absolute Jacobian one, so the change-of-variables theorem applied to its
indicator [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]
gives the same measure from either atlas. Summing over the refinement proves
atlas independence. Countable additivity follows because the chart images of
disjoint Borel sets remain disjoint within each $E_k$ and Lebesgue measure is
countably additive. For the resulting nonnegative array $a_{k\ell}$, both
$\sum_k\sum_\ell a_{k\ell}$ and $\sum_\ell\sum_k a_{k\ell}$ are the
supremum of the same finite subsums of $\{a_{k\ell}\}$, using the
nonnegative extended-sum convention of [[def-measure]]. Hence the sums
reorder and $\Lambda_N$ is a measure with the displayed coordinate density.
Given any finite constant $c_N>0$, define the **labelled reference measure**
$$m_N:=c_N\Lambda_N$$
on $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)$. It is sigma-finite: $Q_N$ is
countable-atlased as just constructed, so it is covered by countably many
cotangent chart images. Each chart image is open in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ and is
covered by the countable family of bounded open boxes with rational endpoints
whose closures lie in that chart image: every point of an open set lies in one
such box. Each box has finite Euclidean Lebesgue measure, and its chart
preimage therefore has finite $m_N$-measure because the Liouville coordinate
density is the constant $c_N$. The countably many chart-box preimages cover
$\Gamma_N$ and establish sigma-finiteness directly, without a sigma-compactness
supplier.
The constant $c_N$ is mathematical normalization data; this definition assigns
no physical unit to it.

For a partition of the particle labels into species classes of sizes
$N_1,\ldots,N_s$, let $G:=S_{N_1}\times\cdots\times S_{N_s}$ act on
$Q_N=Q^N$ by permuting factors within each class and on $T^*Q_N$ by the
cotangent lift. In canonical coordinates each lift permutes corresponding
$q$ and $p$ coordinates, so it preserves $\omega_N$, $\Lambda_N$ and $m_N$.
Let $\Pi_N:\Gamma_N\to\Gamma_N/G$ be
the orbit map, equip the orbit set with the quotient sigma-algebra
$$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quot}}:=\{B\subseteq\Gamma_N/G:\Pi_N^{-1}(B) \text{ is Borel in }\Gamma_N\},$$
and define the **quotient reference measure** by
$$\bar m_N(B):=\frac{1}{\prod_{a=1}^s N_a!}\,m_N(\Pi_N^{-1}(B)).$$
This is a measure because inverse images preserve complements and countable
disjoint unions and $m_N$ is countably additive. The stated invariance makes
it the normalized quotient pushforward. It is a measurable quotient;
no smooth quotient structure at configurations with stabilizers is asserted.
For one species the factor is $1/N!$.

The quotient factor here is mathematical counting data. A physical postulate
determines when labels are operationally indistinguishable and how the
reference scale is interpreted; neither follows from the cotangent geometry.

items.title: Equipartition identity with explicit integrated boundary terms
items.statement:
Let $(Y,\mathcal G,\nu)$ be a sigma-finite measure space, $\beta>0$, and
$H:\mathbb R\times Y\to\mathbb R$ a product-measurable function whose map
$z\mapsto H(z,y)$ is $C^1$ for $\nu$-almost every $y$. Set
$$Z:=\int_{\mathbb R\times Y}e^{-\beta H(z,y)}\,d(z,y)\in(0,\infty),$$
where $d(z,y)$ is Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R$ times $\nu$. Assume
$$\int_{\mathbb R\times Y}|z\partial_zH(z,y)|e^{-\beta H(z,y)}\,d(z,y)<\infty.$$
For $R>0$ let
$$B_R:=\int_Y\bigl(R e^{-\beta H(R,y)}+R e^{-\beta H(-R,y)}\bigr)\,d\nu(y),$$
and assume $B_R\to0$ as $R\to\infty$. Define
$$\langle F\rangle_\beta:=Z^{-1}\int F(z,y)e^{-\beta H(z,y)}\,d(z,y)$$
whenever the integral is absolutely convergent. Then
$$\langle z\partial_zH\rangle_\beta=\beta^{-1}.$$
For finite endpoints $a<b$, assume the endpoint integral below is finite and
put $Z_{[a,b]}:=\int_{[a,b]\times Y}e^{-\beta H}\,d(z,y)$. If
$0<Z_{[a,b]}<\infty$, define
$\langle F\rangle_{[a,b]}:=Z_{[a,b]}^{-1}\int_{[a,b]\times Y}F e^{-\beta H}\,d(z,y)$.
Then the exact boundary identity is
$$\langle z\partial_zH\rangle_{[a,b]}=\beta^{-1}\left(1-Z_{[a,b]}^{-1}\int_Y\bigl(b e^{-\beta H(b,y)}-a e^{-\beta H(a,y)}\bigr)\,d\nu(y)\right),$$

items.title: Statistical states, densities, observables and expectations
items.statement:
Let $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N,m_N)$ be a sigma-finite phase-reference measure
space from [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]; the cotangent construction uses
the stated Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). A **statistical state** is a probability measure
$P$ on $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)$, meaning a countably additive measure with
$P(\Gamma_N)=1$ ([[def-measure]]). A **density** of $P$ relative to $m_N$ is a
measurable $\rho:\Gamma_N\to[0,\infty]$ such that
$$P(A)=\int_A\rho\,dm_N\quad(A\in\mathcal F_N),\qquad \int_{\Gamma_N}\rho\,dm_N=1.$$
Equivalently, $P=\rho\,m_N$ in the definition of a measure with density
([[def-measure-with-density]]); integration against that density has the
meaning supplied by [[thm-integration-against-a-density]]. A state need not
have a density.

An **observable** is a real-valued measurable function
$A:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-extended-real-valued-measurable-function]]).
Its expectation $\langle A\rangle_P:=\int A\,dP$ is used only when $A$ is
integrable, that is, $\int|A|\,dP<\infty$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). Its
variance is
$$\operatorname{Var}_P(A):=\int(A-\langle A\rangle_P)^2\,dP$$
when $A^2$ is integrable. For square-integrable $A,B$, their covariance is
$$\operatorname{Cov}_P(A,B):=\int(A-\langle A\rangle_P)(B-\langle B\rangle_P)\,dP.$$
These expressions are finite under the stated square-integrability
hypotheses. Indeed, $P(\Gamma_N)=1$ makes $1\in L^2(P)$ with norm $1$.
By [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]],
$\int|A|\,dP\le(\int A^2\,dP)^{1/2}$, so the mean of a square-integrable
observable exists. If $a=\langle A\rangle_P$, then
$|A-a|^2\le2A^2+2a^2$ makes $A-a$ square-integrable; the same argument
applies to $B-b$. A second application of that inequality gives
$\int|(A-a)(B-b)|\,dP\le\|A-a\|_2\|B-b\|_2<\infty$.
Thus both the variance and covariance integrals above are well-defined.

If $P=\rho m_N$ and the integrals are defined, these expectations equal
$\int A\rho\,dm_N$ by [[thm-integration-against-a-density]].

A **macrostate map** is a measurable map
$M:(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)\to(Y,\mathcal G)$. Its induced state on $Y$ is
the pushforward $M_*P(B):=P(M^{-1}(B))$ for $B\in\mathcal G$.
A **macrocell** associated with a specified measurable cell $B\in\mathcal G$
is the measurable phase event $C_B:=M^{-1}(B)$; its reference size is
$m_N(C_B)\in[0,\infty]$. A singleton fibre $M^{-1}(\{y\})$ is used as a
macrocell only when $\{y\}\in\mathcal G$. For a specified family
$\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal G$ of cells, an **entropy assignment** means
additional data $S:\mathcal C\to[-\infty,\infty]$; no particular functional
of $m_N(C_B)$ is stipulated here. Neither a cell's reference size nor a
separately chosen entropy assignment is defined to be the expectation or
variance of a microscopic observable.

items.title: Coarea and invariant probability on compact regular phase shells
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Gamma_N=T^*Q_N$ be a cotangent phase space
from [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]], with $\dim Q_N=n$, and let $J\subseteq
\mathbb R$ be open. Let $H:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$ have a $C^2$ coordinate
representative $H\circ\psi^{-1}$ in every canonical cotangent chart $\psi$;
write $dH$ for the resulting differential. Assume
$dH\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$ and suppose $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact for every compact
$K\subset J$. Use the real canonical cotangent coordinates
$z=(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ of
[[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]; this mathematical theorem assigns no
physical units to these coordinates.

For a compact regular energy band, take a finite smooth partition of unity
$\{\chi_a\}$ subordinate to canonical cotangent charts. In a chart where
$\partial_iH\ne0$, write the local energy graph as $z_i=h_a(y,E)$ and define
the **weighted shell measure** on nonnegative Borel $f$ by
$$\mu_E(f):=c_N\sum_a\int f(y,h_a(y,E))\chi_a(y,h_a(y,E))|\partial_iH(y,h_a(y,E))|^{-1}\,dy,$$
where $c_N>0$ is the constant density of the reference measure in canonical
coordinates. Then this definition is independent of the chosen finite chart
partition and equals the chart expression
$$\mu_E(f)=c_N\int_{\Sigma_E}f(z)|\nabla_zH(z)|^{-1}\,dA_z,$$
with $\Sigma_E:=H^{-1}(\{E\})$ and Euclidean area in each real
canonical chart. For every nonnegative Borel $f$ compactly supported in
$H^{-1}(J)$,
$$\int_{\Gamma_N}f\,dm_N=\int_J\mu_E(f)\,dE.$$
If $\Sigma_E$ is nonempty, then $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$ and
$P_E:=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$ is a probability measure. If a Hamiltonian flow map is a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism on a full compact energy band and preserves that band,
then $P_E$ is invariant under that map for every such regular $E$. Critical
levels and noncompact inverse bands are outside this statement. For its
invariance clause, fix a compatible metric on a compact band whose interior
contains the shell; such a metric exists by
[[thm-topological-manifolds-are-metrizable-and-paracompact]].

The same shell measure can be computed after a fixed numerical coordinate
normalization. Choose positive real scales $\ell_j,p_{0j}$ with a common
product $\ell_jp_{0j}=A>0$, and put
$$q^j=\ell_jQ^j,\qquad p_j=p_{0j}P_j,\qquad F(Q,P)=(q,p),\qquad \widetilde H=H\circ F.$$
The reference density becomes $\widehat c_N\,dQ\,dP$ with
$\widehat c_N=c_NA^n$. The graph and weighted-area formulas above then use
$\widetilde H$, its gradient and Euclidean area in $(Q,P)$, and
$\widehat c_N$, with the same energy variable $E$. They describe the
pullback of $\mu_E$, not a different shell law. The pulled-back forms are
$$F^*\lambda=A\sum_jP_j\,dQ^j,\qquad F^*\omega_N=A\sum_jdQ^j\wedge dP_j.$$
For a Hamiltonian trajectory parameterized by its original $t$, the equations
in these coordinates are
$$\frac{dQ^j}{dt}=A^{-1}\partial_{P_j}\widetilde H,\qquad \frac{dP_j}{dt}=-A^{-1}\partial_{Q^j}\widetilde H.$$
This chart normalization does not rescale $H$, $E$ or $t$.

items.title: Classical particle counting and physical observables
items.statement:
For a declared classical model with $N_a$ operationally indistinguishable
particles of each species $a$, label those particles by
$\{(a,i):1\le i\le N_a\}$ on the auxiliary labelled cover, and let
$S_{N_a}$ denote the permutation group of that species' finite label set.
The product group $G=\prod_a S_{N_a}$ acts on the labelled phase space
$\Gamma_N=T^*Q_N$ by the cotangent lifts of within-species permutations. Let
$\Pi_N:\Gamma_N\to\Gamma_N/G$ be its measurable orbit map from
[[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]. Choose $a_0>0$ as a fixed primitive
reference parameter with action units J s; [[def-cm01-units]] supplies its
dimension, not its value or the choice of this parameter. Here $d$ is the
number of spatial dimensions and $N=\sum_aN_a$. No numerical value or
identification of $a_0$ with Planck's constant is imposed.

Use the weighted labelled lift
$$m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}:=\frac{1}{\prod_aN_a!\,a_0^{dN}}\,d\Lambda_N =\frac{1}{\prod_aN_a!\,a_0^{dN}}\,dq\,dp$$
on $\Gamma_N$, where $d\Lambda_N$ is the Liouville density and the last
expression is its coordinate density in canonical charts, with coordinates
read in SI numerical units. The coordinate volume $dq\,dp$ has action
dimension $(\mathrm{J\,s})^{dN}$, so the reference is dimensionless. The
physical quotient reference is
$$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(B):=m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(\Pi_N^{-1}(B))\qquad(B\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quot}}).$$
Thus $m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ is on the labelled cover $\Gamma_N$, and
$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}=(\Pi_N)_*m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ is on
$\Gamma_N/G$; with $c_N=a_0^{-dN}$, the latter is exactly the normalized
quotient reference of [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]].

Physical observables for indistinguishable particles are measurable
$G$-invariant functions $A:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$, equivalently measurable
functions $\bar A$ on the quotient with $A=\bar A\circ\Pi_N$. For every such
observable with an integrable expectation, its integral against
$m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ equals the quotient integral against
$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$. A labelled density represents a physical state on
the quotient only if it is invariant under $G$ almost everywhere with respect
to $m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$; an invariant representative may then be used. In
particular, an indistinguishable-particle Hamiltonian must be invariant under
these permutations (or agree almost everywhere with its permuted versions
when only its Gibbs density is at issue). A label-specific coordinate
statistic on the lift is not itself a quotient observable. Under a
permutation-invariant state its marginal law
can instead be interpreted as the law of a uniformly selected particle within
the same species, or of a uniformly selected coordinate of the same type
within that species. Symmetric sums and averages within each species are
quotient observables.
Calculations of labelled momentum components in
[[pthm-csm-canonical-momentum-equipartition]] use this symmetric labelled
lift, and their permutation-invariant kinetic sums and averages are physical
observables.

If labels are operationally distinguishable, omit the corresponding
permutation factor and use the labelled phase space directly. The convention
is part of the preparation and reference model; it is not deduced from
Hamiltonian mechanics. Whether a quantity is represented by a gauge-dependent
canonical momentum or by a gauge-invariant mechanical momentum is fixed by the
stated model and gauge convention. No quantum exchange law, actual preparation
mechanism, or empirical indistinguishability test is asserted.
items.physical_scope: Finite-N classical phase spaces with explicitly declared species and observationally indistinguishable labels; no derivation of indistinguishability or quantum statistics.

items.title: Dominated exponential normalization and covariance
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,m)$ be a sigma-finite measure space, let $w\ge0$ be
measurable with $m(\{w>0\})>0$, let $r\ge1$ and let
$X=(X_1,\ldots,X_r):\Omega\to\mathbb R^r$ be measurable and finite, and let
$\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^r$ be open. For
each compact $K\subset\Theta$, assume an integrable $G_K$ satisfies
$$w(x)e^{\theta\cdot X(x)}\left(1+\sum_a|X_a(x)|^2\right)\le G_K(x)\quad(\theta\in K).$$
Then $Z(\theta)=\int w e^{\theta\cdot X}\,dm$ is finite, strictly positive
and $C^2$, and the probability density $\rho_\theta=Z(\theta)^{-1}we^{\theta\cdot X}$
defines $dP_\theta=\rho_\theta\,dm$ as in [[def-measure-with-density]].
For any integrable real $A$, write $\langle A\rangle_\theta:=\int A\,dP_\theta$;
for square-integrable real $A,B$, define
$\operatorname{Cov}_\theta(A,B):=\int(A-\langle A\rangle_\theta)(B-\langle B\rangle_\theta)\,dP_\theta$.
These extend the phase-space conventions of
[[def-csm-statistical-state-observable]] to the present measure space.
Then
$$\partial_a\log Z=\langle X_a\rangle_\theta,\qquad \partial_a\partial_b\log Z=\operatorname{Cov}_\theta(X_a,X_b).$$
In particular, the Hessian of $\log Z$ is positive semidefinite.

items.title: Kinetic-plus-potential shell marginals and moments
items.statement:
Let integers $d,N\ge1$ satisfy $n=dN\ge3$. Choose a basis
$b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $\mathbb R^d$ and the full-rank lattice
$\Lambda:=\sum_{i=1}^d\mathbb Zb_i$. The one-particle flat torus is
$Q:=\mathbb R^d/\Lambda$ with its quotient Euclidean metric and
translation-invariant volume $V:=|\det(b_1,\ldots,b_d)|$. Write
$\Lambda^N:=\Lambda\times\cdots\times\Lambda$ ($N$ factors) and set
$Q_N:=Q^N\cong\mathbb R^n/\Lambda^N$, whose position volume is $V^N$.
Use the global parallel cotangent trivialization $\Gamma_N\cong Q_N\times
\mathbb R^n$ and the product of quotient Lebesgue volume $dq$ with fibre
Lebesgue measure $dp$ in the canonical reference
$m_N=c_Ndq\,dp$ of [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]. Let $m_j>0$ for
$1\le j\le n$, and let $U:Q_N\to\mathbb R$ be bounded with a smooth lift
$\widetilde U:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfying
$\widetilde U(x+\lambda)=\widetilde U(x)$ for all $x\in\mathbb R^n$ and
$\lambda\in\Lambda^N$. Set
$$H(q,p)=\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{p_j^2}{2m_j}+U(q),\qquad \alpha=n/2,\qquad C_m=\prod_{j=1}^n\sqrt{2m_j}.$$
Let $B_n$ be the Euclidean volume of the unit ball in $\mathbb R^n$. Fix
an energy $E$ that is a regular value of $H$ and whose shell
$\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$ is nonempty. For every continuous $g:Q_N\to\mathbb R$,
the coarea shell measure from [[thm-csm-regular-shell-coarea]] satisfies
$$\mu_E(g\circ\pi_N)=c_N C_m\alpha B_n\int_{Q_N}g(q)(E-U(q))_+^{\alpha-1}\,dq,$$
where $x_+=\max(x,0)$. Thus the position marginal of $P_E$ has density
proportional to $(E-U)_+^{\alpha-1}$. In the scaled momentum coordinates
$r_j=p_j/\sqrt{2m_j}$, the coarea shell measure over each $q$ with
$E>U(q)$ has fiber factor $dA_r/(2|r|)$ on the sphere
$|r|=\sqrt{E-U(q)}$. Define $\sigma_{E,q}$ as Euclidean surface area on
that sphere divided by its total area. It satisfies
$$\int \frac{p_j^2}{2m_j}\,d\sigma_{E,q}=\frac{E-U(q)}{n},\qquad \int \sum_j\frac{p_j^2}{2m_j}\,dP_E=\int(E-U(q))\,dP_E(q).$$
The result concerns the full kinetic-plus-potential shell; it does not replace
it by a shell of potential energy alone.

items.title: Liouville transport and fine-grained entropy invariance
items.statement:
Let $D\subseteq\Gamma_N$ be an open invariant domain for a $C^2$ Hamiltonian
$H$, and let its actual Hamiltonian flow $\Phi_t:D\to D$ be defined as a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism for each time $t$ considered, with
$\Phi_{-t}=\Phi_t^{-1}$. Let $m_N=c_N\Lambda_N$ be the Liouville
reference measure of [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]. If $P_0=\rho_0m_N$
is a probability state, define its transported density by
$$\rho_t(z)=\rho_0(\Phi_{-t}z).$$
Then $\rho_t$ is normalized and, for every measurable $f$ for which the
integrals exist,
$$\int_D f(z)\rho_t(z)\,dm_N(z)=\int_D f(\Phi_tz)\rho_0(z)\,dm_N(z).$$
If additionally $\int_D|\rho_0\log\rho_0|\,dm_N<\infty$, with
$0\log0:=0$, then the fine-grained reference-relative entropy
$$S(\rho):=-k\int_D\rho\log\rho\,dm_N\quad(k>0)$$
is constant under this transport. This is an identity for the transported
density; it asserts no relaxation, equilibration or entropy increase.

items.title: Canonical thermal preparation
items.statement:
For a fixed $N$, controls $\lambda$, measurable classical Hamiltonian
$H_{N,\lambda}:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, measurable for the
phase Borel sigma-algebra and taking energy values in joules, and the declared
physical reference measure $m_N^{\rm phys}$ of
[[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]], choose a prescribed
thermodynamic-temperature control $T>0$ in kelvins and
$\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in J$^{-1}$ using the SI temperature convention of
[[def-td-si-quantities]]. For every within-species permutation $g\in G$
of [[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]], require
$H_{N,\lambda}(gz)=H_{N,\lambda}(z)$ for $m_N^{\rm phys}$-almost every $z$.
Thus its Gibbs density has an invariant representative and represents a
quotient state under the declared indistinguishable-particle convention.
For operationally distinguishable labels the corresponding group is trivial
and its factorial is omitted, as specified by that convention. If
$$0<Z_N(\beta,\lambda):=\int_{\Gamma_N}e^{-\beta H_{N,\lambda}}\,dm_N^{\rm phys}<\infty,$$
adopt the canonical state with density
$$\rho_{\beta,\lambda}=Z_N(\beta,\lambda)^{-1}e^{-\beta H_{N,\lambda}}$$
relative to $m_N^{\rm phys}$. Set $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$. Normalizability
is a required condition on the chosen model; bounded-below energy alone does
not imply it. This probability law is an adopted preparation, not a
consequence of deterministic mechanics or evidence of laboratory
equilibration.
items.physical_scope: Fixed finite particle number and fixed controls in a classical canonical model with a finite positive partition function; no claim that isolated Hamiltonian dynamics prepares or equilibrates this law.

items.title: Grand canonical particle-exchange preparation
items.statement:
Let $T>0$ be the prescribed temperature control in kelvins,
$\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$, and let the chemical-potential control $\mu$ have
units J per particle under the SI convention
[[def-td-si-quantities]]. In this adopted law, $\mu$ is the energy
coefficient conjugate to the dimensionless sector count $N$ in the weight
$e^{-\beta(H_N-\mu N)}$; no derivative with respect to integer $N$ is used.
For $N\ge1$, let $\Gamma_N$ and its reference
measure be those of [[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]], and let
$$H_N:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$$
be Borel measurable for the sector sigma-algebra
$\mathcal F_N$ generated by the open sets of $\Gamma_N$, with $+\infty$
marking forbidden states, and use the convention
$e^{-\beta(+\infty)}:=0$. In each sector require
$H_N(gz)=H_N(z)$ for $m_N^{\rm phys}$-almost every $z$ and every
within-species permutation $g\in G_N$, with $G_N$ and its action as in
[[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]]. Hence each sector Gibbs
density admits an invariant representative; the factor $e^{\beta\mu N}$
is constant on that sector and preserves this invariance. Operationally
distinguishable labels have trivial permutation factors as in that convention.
Define
the vacuum sector by $\Gamma_0=\{*\}$ with sigma-algebra
$\mathcal F_0=\{\varnothing,\{*\}\}$, reference mass
$m_0^{\mathrm{phys}}(\{*\})=1$, particle number $N=0$, and vacuum Hamiltonian
$H_0(*)=0$. On the disjoint union $\mathcal G:=\bigsqcup_{N=0}^\infty\Gamma_N$,
use the sigma-algebra
$$\mathcal F_{\mathcal G}:=\{A\subseteq\mathcal G:A\cap\Gamma_N\in\mathcal F_N\text{ for every }N\ge0\},$$
where $\mathcal F_N$ is the declared measurable structure on sector $N$, and
the reference measure
$$m^{\mathrm{phys}}(A):=\sum_{N=0}^\infty m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(A\cap\Gamma_N).$$
This disjoint-union reference is sigma-finite because it is a countable sum
of the sigma-finite sector references, including the finite vacuum measure.
Let
$$\Xi(\beta,\mu):=\sum_{N=0}^\infty\int_{\Gamma_N} e^{-\beta(H_N-\mu N)}\,dm_N^{\rm phys}$$
satisfy $0<\Xi<\infty$. Adopt the probability measure on
$(\mathcal G,\mathcal F_{\mathcal G})$ with density
$$\rho(N,z):=\Xi^{-1}e^{-\beta(H_N(z)-\mu N)}$$
relative to $m^{\mathrm{phys}}$. The finiteness condition is
part of the model; it requires control of the sector sum and is not implied
by each finite-sector partition function being finite. Particle-exchange
preparation is an assumption, not a deduction from fixed-$N$ dynamics. Under
the vacuum convention above, the $N=0$ contribution to $\Xi$ is exactly one.
items.physical_scope: Classical particle exchange across countably many finite-N sectors at fixed temperature and chemical potential, only when the grand normalization converges.

items.title: Isothermal-isobaric joint preparation
items.statement:
Fix integers $N,d\ge1$, a prescribed temperature control $T>0$ in kelvins,
$\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ as in [[def-td-si-quantities]], and external pressure
$P_{\rm ext}>0$ in J m$^{-d}$, a fixed dimensionless shape
$Q_1\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ that is Lebesgue measurable, meaning
$Q_1\in\mathcal L(\mathbb R^d)$, and has Lebesgue measure
$|Q_1|_d:=\lambda_d(Q_1)=1$
([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]), and
a positive volume reference $V_0$ in m$^d$. Write
$y=(y_1,\ldots,y_N)\in Q_1^N$, take $dy$ to be product Lebesgue measure on
$Q_1^N$, take $dp$ to be Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^{dN}$, and take
$dV$ to be Lebesgue measure on $(0,\infty)$. Identify
the position domain at volume $V>0$ by $q_i=V^{1/d}y_i$. The Jacobian is
$V^N$, which is the full position-volume factor because $|Q_1|_d=1$. Adopt
the joint reference
$$d\nu_N=\frac{dV}{V_0}\,\frac{V^N\,dy\,dp}{N!a_0^{dN}},$$
where $a_0>0$ is the action reference in J s. The factors $dV/V_0$ and
$V^Ndy\,dp/a_0^{dN}$ are dimensionless. Let
$$H_N:(0,\infty)\times Q_1^N\times\mathbb R^{dN}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$$
be a product-measurable energy-valued Hamiltonian (in joules) for this
reference, with $+\infty$ marking forbidden states. Require
$H_N(V,g\cdot(y,p))=H_N(V,y,p)$ for $\nu_N$-almost every $(V,y,p)$
and every within-species permutation $g$, acting by simultaneous
permutation of the position and momentum particle coordinates. For the
displayed single-species factor this group is $S_N$; for several species it
is $\prod_a S_{N_a}$ as in [[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]].
The volume coordinate is unchanged by this action, so the Gibbs density
admits an invariant representative on the labelled lift. Set
$e^{-\beta(+\infty+P_{\rm ext}V)}:=0$. The product reference
$\nu_N$ is sigma-finite: $Q_1^N$ has finite measure, while $(0,\infty)$ and
$\mathbb R^{dN}$ have countable finite-measure exhaustions; the factor $V^N$
is finite on each set where $V$ is bounded. Assume
$$0<\Delta_N:=\int_{(0,\infty)\times Q_1^N\times\mathbb R^{dN}} e^{-\beta(H_N(V,y,p)+P_{\rm ext}V)}\,d\nu_N<\infty.$$
Adopt the probability density
$$\rho_N(V,y,p):=\Delta_N^{-1}e^{-\beta(H_N(V,y,p)+P_{\rm ext}V)}$$
relative to $\nu_N$. The displayed
$N!$ is the single-species convention; for several indistinguishable species
with fixed counts $N_a$, replace it by $\prod_aN_a!$ as in
[[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]]. The factor $dV/V_0$ is an
explicit volume-reference convention; a different piston state measure gives
a different preparation. This postulate includes no piston kinetic energy
unless it is explicitly included in the Hamiltonian, and does not claim a
smooth wall dynamics.
items.physical_scope: Fixed finite particle number with a classical shape-scaled domain and a declared uniform dV/V0 volume prior; alternative piston measures define different preparations.

items.title: Regular full-shell or finite-band preparation
items.statement:
For the full-shell branch, assume the Axiom of Choice required by the
mathematical supplier [[thm-csm-regular-shell-coarea]]. Let
$H:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$ have a $C^2$ coordinate representative in every
canonical cotangent chart. Require $H(gz)=H(z)$ for every $z\in\Gamma_N$
and every within-species permutation $g\in G$ with the cotangent action
specified by [[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]]. This symmetry
condition applies to both the shell and finite-band branches; ambient
almost-everywhere symmetry alone would not specify a law on an individual
zero-volume shell. Suppose there is an open interval $J\ni E$ on
which $dH\ne0$ and for which $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact whenever $K\subset J$ is
compact. For a nonempty regular shell
$\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$, the cited theorem gives finite positive coarea mass
$0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$; adopt the microcanonical state
$$P_E=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$$
as the probability law for the specified preparation. Here $\mu_E$ is the
shell measure disintegrating the declared phase reference over energy; its
construction and hypotheses are exactly those in that theorem. The constant
$c_N$ in the mathematical reference is chosen to match the fixed-$N$ physical
reference of [[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]]; the normalization
defining $P_E$ also cancels a common positive rescaling of that reference.

For a physical application, choose fixed conjugate reference scales
$\ell_j,p_{0j}>0$ in each cotangent chart, of the respective coordinate and
conjugate-momentum units, with $\ell_jp_{0j}=A>0$ the same action scale for
all $j$. For Cartesian positions these units are m and kg m s$^{-1}$;
other generalized coordinates have their own declared conjugate units. Put
$Q^j=q^j/\ell_j$, $P_j=p_j/p_{0j}$ and
$\widetilde H(Q,P)=H(q,p)$. These coordinates are dimensionless, while
$\widetilde H$ and $E$ remain in J. The actual reference Jacobian gives
$$dm_N^{\rm phys}=\frac{(A/a_0)^n}{\prod_sN_s!}\,dQ\,dP,\qquad n=dN.$$
Use this transformed constant in the shell theorem; in particular
$\mu_E^{\rm phys}(1)$ has units J$^{-1}$. The weighted shell area and
gradient are computed in these dimensionless coordinates, not by adding
squares of SI position and momentum derivatives of different dimensions.
The canonical forms pull back to $A\sum_jP_jdQ^j$ and
$A\sum_jdQ^j\wedge dP_j$. Thus physical time $t$ in seconds obeys
$$\frac{dQ^j}{dt}=A^{-1}\partial_{P_j}\widetilde H,\qquad \frac{dP_j}{dt}=-A^{-1}\partial_{Q^j}\widetilde H.$$
Equivalently the Hamiltonian for the normalized mathematical two-form and
the same time is $\widetilde H/A$, in s$^{-1}$. If one also chooses an
energy reference $E_*>0$ in J, then only with
$\widehat H=\widetilde H/E_*$ and $\tau=E_*t/A$ do the fully dimensionless
equations become $dQ^j/d\tau=\partial_{P_j}\widehat H$ and
$dP_j/d\tau=-\partial_{Q^j}\widehat H$. This is an explicit reexpression of
the same trajectories and physical clock. It changes neither the adopted
shell or band preparation nor the physical Hamiltonian. For dimensionless
shell energy $e=E/E_*$, the shell measures transform as
$\mu_e^{\rm num}=E_*\mu_{E_*e}^{\rm phys}$ so that the coarea integral is
unchanged.


Alternatively, for a specified compact regular energy band $B\subset J$ with
$$0<m_N^{\rm phys}(H^{-1}(B))=\int_B\mu_E^{\rm phys}(1)\,dE<\infty,$$
one may adopt the normalized restricted physical reference
$$P_B(A)=\frac{m_N^{\rm phys}(A\cap H^{-1}(B))}{m_N^{\rm phys}(H^{-1}(B))}$$
for each measurable phase event $A$. Here $m_N^{\rm phys}$ is the declared
fixed-$N$ reference of
[[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]], and
$\mu_E^{\rm phys}$ is its coarea measure; choosing this physical positive
constant in [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]] scales both measures in the
coarea identity equally. This is a distinct finite-band
preparation, uniform relative to phase volume in the band. Restricting either
law to a dynamically accessible invariant subset or imposing further
conserved quantities defines another preparation and requires a separately
specified measure. Neither law nor ergodicity is deduced from deterministic
Hamiltonian evolution.
items.physical_scope: Fixed-N classical models with a nonempty compact regular energy shell or a finite compact regular energy band under the declared phase reference; the shell branch carries its exact full-AC mathematical premise, and neither branch infers ergodicity or equilibration.

items.title: Reference-relative entropy and Gibbs variational inequality
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,m)$ be a measure space and let $p,q$ be probability
densities relative to $m$, with $q>0$ almost everywhere on $\{p>0\}$. Define
the relative entropy
$$D(p\Vert q):=\int_{\{p>0\}}p\log(p/q)\,dm,$$
allowing $+\infty$. Then $D(p\Vert q)\ge0$, and equality holds exactly
when $p=q$ almost everywhere. For arbitrary probability densities, extend
$D(p\Vert q)$ to $+\infty$ if $\int_{\{q=0\}}p\,dm>0$.
In particular, let $H$ be extended-real measurable, finite $p$-almost
everywhere, let $\beta>0$, and suppose
$$0<Z=\int e^{-\beta H}dm<\infty,\quad q=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta H},\quad \int p|H|dm<\infty,\quad \int|p\log p|dm<\infty.$$
For $S[p]:=-k\int p\log p\,dm$ and $F:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$, with $k>0$
and $\beta kT=1$, one has
$$D(p\Vert q)=\beta\bigl(\langle H\rangle_p-F-TS[p]\bigr)\ge0.$$
Write $\mathcal A$ for the probability densities satisfying these finite
energy and absolute entropy conditions. For every measurable $H$ with the
stated positive finite $Z$, define the **extended relative free energy** on
all probability densities by
$$\mathcal F_{\rm ext}[p]:=F+\beta^{-1}D(p\Vert q)\in[F,+\infty].$$
It agrees with $\langle H\rangle_p-TS[p]$ on $\mathcal A$ and has the
unique minimizer $q$, up to almost-everywhere equality, even when the
separate energy and entropy integrals of $q$ are not finite. Moreover,
$$\inf_{p\in\mathcal A}\bigl(\langle H\rangle_p-TS[p]\bigr)=F.$$
This infimum is attained if and only if
$\int q|H|dm<\infty$ and $\int|q\log q|dm<\infty$; in that case its
unique minimizer is $q$. Otherwise no density in $\mathcal A$ attains the
infimum. Products with a zero density are taken as zero on the forbidden
set, and densities may be redefined on null sets. These mathematical
claims do not derive a physical preparation.

items.title: Canonical momentum distribution and equipartition
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], as in the cotangent phase-reference convention. Let $d,N\ge1$ and put $n=dN$. Use the ambient smooth configuration manifold
$\mathbb R^n=(\mathbb R^d)^N$ and its cotangent phase space
$\Gamma_N=T^*\mathbb R^n\cong\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n$ with product
Lebesgue measure $dq\,dp$ in canonical coordinates. Let the allowed
one-particle position region $C\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact and Lebesgue
measurable with $0<|C|_d<\infty$, and set $C_N=C^N$ with product Lebesgue
measure and volume $|C|_d^N$. Let $U_C:C_N\to\mathbb R$ be bounded and
measurable, invariant under permutations of the $N$ particle labels, and
interpret measurability here with respect to completed Lebesgue measure on
$C_N$. Choose a bounded, permutation-invariant Borel representative
$\widetilde U_C$ equal to $U_C$ almost everywhere, as constructed in step 1.1,
and extend it to $U:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ by
$U=\widetilde U_C$ on $C_N$ and $U=+\infty$ outside $C_N$. The canonical
state is defined on the Borel phase reference. Its extension to the completed
phase-reference sigma-algebra agrees with the density formed from the original
$U_C$ and is independent of the Borel representative. In particular, the density vanishes
outside the allowed finite-volume configuration region. The particles have
common mass $m>0$.
Adopt the canonical preparation of
[[post-csm-canonical-preparation]] with the physical reference convention of
[[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]], Hamiltonian
$$K(p):=\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{p_j^2}{2m},\qquad H(q,p):=K(p)+U(q),\qquad p\in\mathbb R^n,$$
and $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$. Then the partition function is finite and
positive, and the momentum components are independent centered Gaussians
with variance $m/\beta=mk_BT$. In particular,
$$\left\langle\frac{p_j^2}{2m}\right\rangle=\frac{1}{2\beta} =\frac{k_BT}{2},\qquad \langle K\rangle=\frac{n k_BT}{2}.$$
These are conditional deductions of the chosen canonical model.
items.physical_scope: Finite classical canonical model with quadratic unconstrained momenta and bounded potential on a finite-volume configuration space; excludes constraints, relativistic dispersion, and empirical equilibration.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete author-hosted lecture-note chapter 2, §§2.2.1 and 2.3
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, complete course text, §4.4.6

items.title: Canonical energy and fluctuation responses
items.statement:
For the canonical preparation [[post-csm-canonical-preparation]], write
$H:=H_{N,\lambda}:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ for its measurable
Hamiltonian and $m:=m_N^{\rm phys}$ for its reference. With these data fixed
independently of $T$, let $Z(\beta)=\int e^{-\beta H}dm$ be finite and positive on an open
interval of $\beta>0$. If $H$ may equal $+\infty$, put
$S_H:=\{x:H(x)<\infty\}$, restrict $m$ to this measurable set, and evaluate
energy moments on $S_H$; the canonical weight is zero outside it, and the
restricted measure remains sigma-finite. In this statement $U$ and
$\operatorname{Var}(H)$ are the expectation and variance of $H|_{S_H}$.
Assume the
local envelope hypotheses of
[[thm-csm-exponential-normalization-covariance]] hold for the finite-valued
statistic $X=H|_{S_H}$ and $\theta=-\beta$ on the restricted measure space.
Under the canonical preparation
[[post-csm-canonical-preparation]], the mean energy $U=\langle H\rangle$ obeys
$$\partial_\beta\log Z=-U,\qquad \partial_\beta U=-\operatorname{Var}(H),\qquad C_V:=\partial_TU=\frac{\operatorname{Var}(H)}{k_BT^2}\ge0,$$
where $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ and $C_V$ is the model heat capacity at the fixed
controls. This is a finite-model response identity, not an empirical claim.
items.physical_scope: Finite canonical model with fixed Hamiltonian, reference measure, particle number and controls on an open temperature interval satisfying local exponential-moment envelopes; no thermodynamic-limit claim.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete author-hosted lecture-note chapter 1, §1.3.2
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, complete course text, §4.4.7

items.title: Ensemble entropy and potential identities
items.statement:
Adopt the canonical, grand and isothermal-isobaric preparations of
[[post-csm-canonical-preparation]], [[post-csm-grand-preparation]] and
[[post-csm-isobaric-preparation]]. Assume their positive finite normalizers,
finite first moments and integrable $\rho\log\rho$, and assume the local
parameter envelopes of [[thm-csm-exponential-normalization-covariance]] for
each normalizer's sufficient statistics. If a Hamiltonian may be
$+\infty$, restrict its reference to the measurable set where it is finite;
the Gibbs density is zero off that set, and the restricted reference remains
sigma-finite. Thus every statistic passed to the exponential theorem is
finite real-valued. In each preparation, write $U:=\langle H\rangle$ for the
mean Hamiltonian; on the grand disjoint union let $\mathsf N$ be the sector
index and write $\bar N:=\langle\mathsf N\rangle$. Define the
reference-relative entropy by
$S=-k_B\int\rho\log\rho\,dm$ using the exact joint reference of each
preparation. Then the finite canonical free energy, grand potential and
isothermal-isobaric potential satisfy
$$F=-k_BT\log Z=U-TS,\qquad dF=-S\,dT$$
at fixed canonical model and reference;
$$\Omega=-k_BT\log\Xi=U-TS-\mu\bar N,\qquad d\Omega=-S\,dT-\bar N\,d\mu;$$
and, with $B=H+P_{\rm ext}V$,
$$G_{\rm isoP}=-k_BT\log\Delta=\langle H\rangle+P_{\rm ext}\langle V\rangle-TS, \qquad dG_{\rm isoP}=-S\,dT+\langle V\rangle\,dP_{\rm ext}.$$
For every normalized competing density $p$ with the same reference and the
finite energy and entropy conditions of
[[thm-csm-relative-gibbs-variational-principle]], one also has
$\langle H\rangle_p-TS[p]\ge F$, with equality exactly at the canonical
density almost everywhere.
The differentials hold at fixed remaining model data; integer $N$ is not a
differentiable variable. The identities do not assert thermodynamic-limit
equivalence or derive any preparation from ignorance.
items.physical_scope: Finite canonical, grand and isothermal-isobaric preparations with finite entropy and energy moments and differentiable normalizers; identities use the explicitly chosen reference measures and fixed microscopic models.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete author-hosted lecture-note chapter 1, §§1.3–1.4
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, complete course text, §§4.4–4.7

items.title: Grand responses in beta and chemical potential
items.statement:
For the grand preparation [[post-csm-grand-preparation]], write
let $\mathcal G$ and $m^{\rm phys}$ be its disjoint-union state space and
reference, define $H(N,z):=H_N(z)$ on sector $\Gamma_N$, and define the
particle-number statistic $\mathsf N(N,z):=N$. Write $m_N$ for
$m_N^{\rm phys}$ in the sector sum, so
$$\Xi(\beta,\mu)=\sum_N\int e^{-\beta H_N+\beta\mu N}\,dm_N.$$
Here $\beta>0$ and $\mu$ has units J per particle. Let
$S_H:=\{(N,z)\in\mathcal G:H_N(z)<\infty\}$, restrict $m^{\rm phys}$ to this
measurable set, and compute energy moments there; the grand weight is zero
outside it and the restricted measure is sigma-finite. Assume the local
envelopes of [[thm-csm-exponential-normalization-covariance]] hold uniformly
on this restricted space for its finite-valued sufficient statistics $H$
and $\mathsf N$; expectations written $\langle N\rangle$ refer to
$\mathsf N$.
Then
$$\partial_\eta\log\Xi=\langle N\rangle,\quad \partial_\eta^2\log\Xi=\operatorname{Var}(N),\quad \eta=\beta\mu,$$
and, at fixed $\mu$,
$$-\partial_\beta\log\Xi=\langle H-\mu N\rangle,\qquad \partial_\mu\langle N\rangle=\beta\operatorname{Var}(N),\qquad \partial_\beta\langle N\rangle|_\mu=-\operatorname{Cov}(N,H-\mu N).$$
The covariance is computed in the full number-exchanging state. No
fixed-$N$ derivative or thermodynamic-limit identification is implied.
items.physical_scope: Grand preparation on a countable disjoint union with local uniform exponential-moment envelopes for energy and particle number; all derivatives are finite-model derivatives.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete author-hosted lecture-note chapter 1, §1.4
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, complete course text, §4.7

items.title: Isobaric volume and enthalpy fluctuations
items.statement:
For the joint preparation of [[post-csm-isobaric-preparation]], write $H=H_N$
for its Hamiltonian and set $B=H+P_{\rm ext}V$. Suppose the local
exponential envelopes hold for
$(B,V)$ on the measurable finite-energy set $S_H:=\{H<\infty\}$, with the
joint reference restricted to $S_H$. The Gibbs weight is zero off $S_H$;
there $B$ and $V$ are finite real-valued statistics and the restricted
reference remains sigma-finite. At fixed $T>0$ and $P_{\rm ext}>0$,
$$\partial_{P_{\rm ext}}\log\Delta=-\beta\langle V\rangle,\qquad \partial_{P_{\rm ext}}\langle V\rangle=-\beta\operatorname{Var}(V),$$
$$-\partial_\beta\log\Delta\big|_{P_{\rm ext}}=\langle B\rangle,\qquad C_P:=\partial_T\langle B\rangle\big|_{P_{\rm ext}} =\frac{\operatorname{Var}(B)}{k_BT^2}\ge0.$$
When $\langle V\rangle>0$, the model isothermal compressibility
$\kappa_T:=-\langle V\rangle^{-1}\partial_{P_{\rm ext}}\langle V\rangle$
equals $\beta\operatorname{Var}(V)/\langle V\rangle$. These are finite
preparation responses for the specified $dV/V_0$ reference; they need not
equal macroscopic response functions absent an additional limit argument.
items.physical_scope: Finite isothermal-isobaric preparation with fixed declared joint reference, positive temperature and pressure, and uniform local envelopes for volume and enthalpy moments.

items.title: Static electromagnetic coupling and typed canonical momentum
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be nonempty, bounded and open with compact
closure, and let $U$ be an open neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$. Let the
static scalar potential be $\varphi:U\to\mathbb R$ and the static vector
potential be $A:U\to\mathbb R^3$, both of class $C^2$. Let $m>0$ kg, and let
$q_{\rm p}\in\mathbb R$ C be the particle's signed charge; this model
parameter is distinct from the exact elementary-charge constant $e$ in
[[def-em-si-conventions]]. Let velocity $v\in\mathbb R^3$ have units
m s$^{-1}$. The adopted
single-particle Lagrangian is the function
$$L:\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R,\qquad L(x,v)=\tfrac12m|v|^2+q_{\rm p}A(x)\cdot v-q_{\rm p}\varphi(x),$$
with $A$ in T m and $\varphi$ in V, as in
[[def-em-si-conventions]]. Its Legendre momentum is
$$p:=\partial_vL=mv+q_{\rm p}A(x),$$
so for every $(x,p)\in T^*\Omega\cong\Omega\times\mathbb R^3$ the inverse is
$v=(p-q_{\rm p}A(x))/m$. The **mechanical momentum** is
$\pi:=p-q_{\rm p}A(x)=mv$; the **canonical momentum** is the cotangent coordinate
$p$ of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]. The Legendre transform
$H=p\cdot v-L$, in the convention of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]], is therefore
$$H(x,p)=\frac{|p-q_{\rm p}A(x)|^2}{2m}+q_{\rm p}\varphi(x).$$
At fixed $x$, the velocity derivative has linear part $mI_3$, so the
displayed affine momentum map has the explicit inverse
$v=(p-q_{\rm p}A(x))/m$. Substitution into $p\cdot v-L$ cancels the two
$q_{\rm p}A\cdot v$ terms and gives $\tfrac12m|v|^2+q_{\rm p}\varphi$; using the inverse
gives the displayed Hamiltonian. The supplier [[def-cm12-hamiltonian]]
provides the $p\cdot v-L$ convention for its hyperregular $K-U$ mechanical
presentation; the inverse branch for this velocity-linear electromagnetic
coupling is the local calculation above, not a consequence of that supplier's
$K-U$ scope. The units are $[q_{\rm p}A]=$ kg m s$^{-1}$,
$[q_{\rm p}\varphi]=$ J, and
$[H]=$ J.

For a time-independent gauge function $\chi:U\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^3$
(units V s), adopt the
static convention of [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]:
$A_\chi=A+\nabla\chi$ and $\varphi_\chi=\varphi$. The corresponding
canonical-coordinate change is
$T_\chi(x,p)=(x,p+q_{\rm p}\nabla\chi(x))$; the
mechanical momentum is unchanged under this paired transformation. This
definition specifies an external-potential model only and asserts no
existence of a global potential representation on arbitrary regions.
items.physical_scope: Single nonrelativistic charged particle in a bounded spatial region with prescribed static C2 electromagnetic potentials; excludes source dynamics, field energy, radiation and quantum effects.

references.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, complete author-hosted lecture notes, §3.2
David Tong, Classical Dynamics, complete author-hosted lecture notes, §4.1.2

items.title: Finite canonical partition is invariant under static electromagnetic gauge changes
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be nonempty bounded open with compact
closure, $m>0$, and $q_{\rm p}\in\mathbb R$ the signed particle charge in
coulombs, as defined in [[def-csm-static-gauge-coupled-particle-model]] and
distinct from its exact elementary-charge constant $e$. Let $a_0>0$ be an
action reference and $\beta>0$ have units J$^{-1}$. Let $A,\varphi$ satisfy
the smoothness assumptions of
[[def-csm-static-gauge-coupled-particle-model]], with $\varphi$ bounded.
Adopt the canonical preparation
[[post-csm-canonical-preparation]] and the single-particle reference
convention [[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]] relative to
$dx\,dp/a_0^3$. Then
$$Z_\beta=\frac{1}{a_0^3}\int_\Omega\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-\beta H(x,p)}dp\,dx =\frac1{a_0^3}\left(\frac{2\pi m}{\beta}\right)^{3/2} \int_\Omega e^{-\beta q_{\rm p}\varphi(x)}dx$$
is finite and positive. If $\chi\in C^3$ is time-independent and
$A_\chi=A+\nabla\chi$, $\varphi_\chi=\varphi$, then the paired canonical
coordinate map $T_\chi(x,p)=(x,p+q_{\rm p}\nabla\chi(x))$ satisfies
$$Z_{\beta,\chi}=Z_\beta.$$
It carries the canonical probability to the transformed canonical
probability and leaves the expectation of every integrable measurable
observable of $(x,\pi)$ unchanged, where $\pi=p-q_{\rm p}A(x)$. The result is a
conditional prediction of the adopted static model, not an experimental
observation.
items.physical_scope: Finite one-particle canonical model on a bounded region with static smooth potentials and a fixed action reference; only time-independent gauge changes are covered, with no claim of field dynamics or empirical realization.

title: Classical configuration, phase and reference spaces — Examples

items.title: Finite-size mixing and distinguishability conventions
items.statement:
Take two initially separate equal-volume boxes, each containing $N\ge1$
particles of the same mass $m>0$ at the same $T>0$, with ideal Hamiltonian
$K=\sum p_j^2/(2m)$. Adopt the classical reference with $N!$ counting for
indistinguishable labels and fixed action reference $a_0>0$. Removing the
partition while fixing total particle number $2N$ gives
$$\frac{\Delta S_{\rm identical}}{k_B} =\log\!\left(\frac{4^N(N!)^2}{(2N)!}\right)>0,$$
whereas for two distinguishable species with fixed $N$ of each,
$$\frac{\Delta S_{\rm species}}{k_B}=2N\log2.$$
The probability under the final identical-particle positional law of finding
exactly $N$ particles in each half is $\binom{2N}{N}/4^N$, the reciprocal
factor inside the logarithm above. The identical-particle entropy change is
$O(k_B\log(N+1))$, hence sublinear in $N$; no exact zero at finite $N$ is
claimed. For the distinguishable-species comparison, initially confine species
$A$ (exactly $N$ particles) to the first box and species $B$ (exactly $N$) to
the second; after removing the partition, each species can occupy the full
volume $2V$.
items.physical_scope: Exact finite-N calculation for two equal ideal-gas compartments at equal temperature; distinguishes adopted indistinguishable-label and fixed-species conventions and reports no empirical observation.

items.title: Full ideal-gas shell moments and entropy conventions
items.statement:
Let integers $d,N\ge1$ satisfy $n=dN\ge3$. Take a flat one-particle torus
$Q=\mathbb R^d/\Lambda$, where $\Lambda=\sum_{i=1}^d\mathbb Zb_i$ for a
basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $\mathbb R^d$ and
$V:=|\det(b_1,\ldots,b_d)|>0$, and set
$Q_N=Q^N\cong\mathbb R^n/\Lambda^N$, of position volume $V^N$. Use equal
masses $m>0$, Hamiltonian $H=\sum_{j=1}^np_j^2/(2m)$ and reference
$dq\,dp/(N!a_0^n)$ with fixed action scale $a_0>0$. For $E>0$, write
$\alpha=n/2$. The density of shell measure is
$$D(E)=\frac{V^N(2m)^{n/2}\alpha B_n}{N!a_0^n}E^{\alpha-1},$$
where $B_n$ is the volume of the unit ball in $\mathbb R^n$. Under the full
shell preparation, $K=E$ exactly and each quadratic momentum component has
mean $E/n$. Define the cumulative phase volume below energy $E$ by
$W(E):=m_N^{\rm phys}(\{H<E\})$. Choose an energy reference $E_0>0$ in
joules and a positive phase-volume reference $W_0$ in the same units as
$W(E)$. The reference $dq\,dp/(N!a_0^n)$ is dimensionless, so $W(E)$ and
$W_0$ are dimensionless and $E_0D(E)$ is dimensionless. The shell entropy
$S_{\rm sh}=k_B\log(E_0D(E))$ and cumulative volume entropy
$S_{\rm vol}=k_B\log(W(E)/W_0)$ have derivatives
$$\partial_E S_{\rm sh}=k_B\frac{\alpha-1}{E},\qquad \partial_E S_{\rm vol}=k_B\frac{\alpha}{E}.$$
They differ by $k_B/E$ at finite $n$; neither convention is selected by this
calculation.
items.physical_scope: Finite ideal gas on a compact flat configuration torus at positive regular shell energy; compares two explicitly defined entropy conventions without asserting which one is physically preferred.

items.title: Exact ideal-gas canonical and grand laws
items.statement:
Let $d,N\ge1$, position volume $V>0$, particle mass $m>0$, fixed action
reference $a_0>0$, and $\beta>0$. For
$H_N=\sum_{j=1}^{dN}p_j^2/(2m)$ with position region of volume $V^N$ and
reference $dq\,dp/(N!a_0^{dN})$, put
$$\lambda_T=a_0\sqrt{\frac{\beta}{2\pi m}}\quad\text{and}\quad Z_N=\frac{(V/\lambda_T^d)^N}{N!}.$$
Then $U=dN/(2\beta)$, $\operatorname{Var}(H_N)=dN/(2\beta^2)$ and
$C_V=dNk_B/2$. With chemical potential $\mu$, set
$a=e^{\beta\mu}V/\lambda_T^d$. The grand normalizer and particle law are
$$\Xi=e^a,\qquad \mathbb P(N=j)=e^{-a}\frac{a^j}{j!},\qquad \mathbb E[N]=\operatorname{Var}(N)=a.$$
Conditioned on $N$, the phase state is the canonical one above. These exact
identities concern the adopted finite classical preparation. The component
factorization is stated in labelled momentum coordinates on the symmetric
lift; each single-coordinate marginal is the law of a uniformly selected
degree of freedom, while permutation-invariant sums and averages are the
quotient observables.
items.physical_scope: Finite-N monatomic classical ideal gas in a bounded position region, with a countable grand-canonical number law; excludes quantum exchange and empirical validation.

items.title: Exact finite ideal-gas volume fluctuations
items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$, $d\ge1$, $n=dN$, $m>0$, $a_0>0$, $V_0>0$, $T>0$ and
$P_{\rm ext}>0$. Use the unit-Lebesgue-volume shape $Q_1\subset\mathbb R^d$
and scaled coordinates $y\in Q_1^N$, $p\in\mathbb R^n$ of
[[post-csm-isobaric-preparation]], with physical positions
$q_i=V^{1/d}y_i$. Define the kinetic energy and Hamiltonian by
$$K(p):=\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{p_j^2}{2m},\qquad H_N(V,y,p):=K(p).$$
In the adopted joint reference $dV/V_0$ times the scaled
position-momentum reference, the weight is $V^N e^{-\beta(K+P_{\rm ext}V)}$.
Its normalization is
$$\Delta_N=\frac{1}{V_0a_0^n} \left(\frac{2\pi m}{\beta}\right)^{n/2} \frac{1}{(\beta P_{\rm ext})^{N+1}}.$$
The volume mean and variance and mean enthalpy are
$$\langle V\rangle=\frac{N+1}{\beta P_{\rm ext}},\qquad \operatorname{Var}(V)=\frac{N+1}{(\beta P_{\rm ext})^2},\qquad \langle K+P_{\rm ext}V\rangle=\frac{n/2+N+1}{\beta}.$$
The extra one in the finite-$N$ volume factor follows from the stated
$dV/V_0$ prior; it is not a universal piston correction.
items.physical_scope: Fixed-N ideal gas in the declared dV/V0 isothermal-isobaric preparation with positive external pressure; excludes alternative piston priors and experimental claims.
